explanation: Function templates in C++ enable the creation of generic functions that can operate with different data types without rewriting code for each type. They are used to promote code reusability and type safety by allowing functions to be parameterized with types, which are specified at compile time. This feature is fundamental in generic programming, facilitating the development of flexible and efficient code that adapts to various data types.
syntax: template <typename TypeParameter> ReturnType FunctionName(Parameters) { /* function body */ }
example_explanation: This example defines a function template 'swap' that can swap the values of two variables of any type T. In 'main', the template is instantiated twice: once with integers and once with doubles. This demonstrates how function templates enable writing a single generic function that works with multiple data types, exemplifying the core concept of template programming in C++.
